And we stress that protecting coastal areas, maritime regions, and the protection of infrastructure calls upon us to work together in solidarity based on science, technology, and the available data to make societies more resilient and prepared to face the challenge. The challenge that faces us today makes it incumbent upon us not to let the scarcity of resources a reason for not doing what is required. We promote climate financing, the transfer of technology, early planning, and plans of adaptation in accordance with national interests and requirements of each state. We also stress the importance of the continuing work of the United Nations and other important institutions in establishing long-term partnerships that give priority to the most affected, protect their lands, their identity, and their cultures in a framework of solidarity and cooperation. In conclusion, we look forward for our meeting today to translating our commitments into actual action and further steps by the international community to face rising sea levels out of a sense of responsibility towards future generations and out of our belief that such a challenge requires the international community to work as hard as possible not to leave anyone behind. Thank you.
I thank the representative of Kuwait, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the Czech Republic.

Thank you, Mr. Chair. The Czech Republic aligns itself with the statement on behalf of the European Union and its member states. We stand in solidarity with countries on the front line and support strengthened international cooperation on climate mitigation and adaptation, resilience building, and sustainable development. Czech development cooperation projects focused on environmental protection, water management, and climate resilience in partner countries, drawing on Czech expertise and practical solutions. We thank the distinguished representative of the Czech Republic. And I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Japan.

I thank the distinguished representative of Switzerland, and I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Sri Lanka.

Thank you, Mr. President, Excellencies, distinguished delegates. Sri Lanka welcomes the adoption of the declaration on sea level rise at this high-level plenary meeting. National observations already indicate sea level rise of approximately 2.5 to 3.1 millimeters per year around Sri Lanka. Projections point to a possible rise of between 0.2 and 0.6 meters by 2050. For a densely populated island nation, these are not abstract figures. Low-lying areas along our coast face heightened exposure to inundation, coastal erosion, salinity, intrusion, and displacement. Sea level rise threatens coastal settlements, infrastructure, fisheries, and aquaculture, agricultural land, drinking water sources, tourism assets, and critical coastal ecosystems, impacting heavily on coastal fishing, farming communities, and vulnerable groups. I would like to express my appreciation to all participants for their valuable insights and contributions to today's deliberations. The approval today of the concise, action-oriented, and intergovernmentally negotiated declaration entitled UN Declaration on Sea Level Rise, agreed by consensus, has shifted the international response from fragmented initiatives towards sustained, coordinated, and adequately financed action.
